brief: Deutsche Bank upgrades Tech back to overweight, three weeks after downgrading it to neutral on unfavorable risk-reward. Tech has since underperformed the S&P 500 by over 16pp, falling 11% while the broader index rose almost 6%, pushing relative performance to the bottom of a decade-long trend channel, a level it has V-turned from five times in the last 2.5 years. Tech positioning has dropped from elevated to neutral, now consistent with roughly 10% earnings growth versus Q3's actual 47% and the 36% consensus expects next year, which DB reads as pricing in AI-demand risk and post-midterm regulatory scrutiny. Such rotations have historically seen Tech rise 32% and the S&P 500 16% over the following three months. Separately, DB argues broader positioning still lags earnings growth: large-cap positioning is at the 66th percentile but discretionary positioning alone is only 48th, versus Q3 growth of 31% yoy (12% ex Tech and Energy, 14.4% for the median company); positioning outside Tech is just the 6th percentile and small-caps the 22nd. On midterm and geopolitical risk, DB argues much is priced in already, citing oil 65% above fair value and a Brent curve as backwardated as prior supply-shock episodes.
